text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Asian livestock researchers held a meeting in Hanoi to devise a plan to exploit regional industry potential and establish cooperation between national livestock research systems in Asian countries.
-- The number of female deputies in the National Assembly, elections to which will be held on July 20, will rise by 20 percent thanks to amendments to the electoral law.
-- U.S Craft Corporation and Vietnam Steel Corporation have agreed to carry out a feasibility study on a $300-million Direct Reduction Iron steel smelter project.
-- The government has issued a decree aimed at tightening control over residential registration for all Vietnamese citizens.
-- Vietnam and Sweden have signed accords on scientific research and environmental management.
-- Dr Nguyen Khac Vien, an intellectual and writer on political and social issues, died last week in Hanoi at the age of 84.
-- The travel time on the North-South express train will be cut to 34 hours from 36 hours from May 19.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet will visit Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Italy and Hungary from May 20 to 28 to discuss measures to strengthen cooperation and bilateral relations.
-- Vietnam expects to export 3.5 million tonnes of rice in 1997. The country has exported 998,000 tonnes of rice so far this year.
